evals.prompt: Take Claude Code session 11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555, fork and compact it without touching the original, and create a portable Markdown handoff for Codex.
evals.expected_output: Uses the bundled handoff operation, preserves the source session, and produces a Markdown artifact with source/fork provenance and sanitized handoff context.
assertions: The source session ID remains distinct from the reported fork session ID.
The source transcript is unchanged or has only append-only concurrent activity.
The source picker membership is unchanged and the print-mode fork is not indexed.
The source-recorded working directory is informational and compaction uses an isolated temporary directory by default.
The output contains source and fork provenance plus a handoff-context section.
Claude-specific resume boilerplate is absent from the portable context.

evals.prompt: This transcript has already been compacted. Export its latest summary locally for Cursor; do not make another Claude API request.
evals.expected_output: Uses the bundled extract operation and emits a portable artifact without invoking Claude Code.
assertions: The extract operation succeeds without running a Claude subprocess.
When several compactions exist, the artifact contains the latest summary.
The intended destination is recorded as Cursor.

evals.prompt: I want to see exactly what command would be run to hand this hidden Claude session to another harness, but don't fork or spend any tokens yet.
evals.expected_output: Uses the create operation with --dry-run, resolves the transcript and cwd, and does not invoke compaction.
assertions: The resolved command contains --resume, --fork-session, and /compact.
No new transcript is created.
The source transcript's recorded working directory is reported as informational but is not used as an execution requirement.

evals.prompt: Before we spend tokens on a huge export, give me a read-only assessment of this long-running Claude session: dates, transcript size, prompt and tool counts, number of compactions, and the pre/post-token timeline.
evals.expected_output: Uses the bundled summary operation to generate a local lifetime report without invoking Claude or modifying the source.
assertions: No Claude subprocess is invoked and no fork transcript is created.
The report includes session dates, transcript scale, filtered user-prompt and assistant-record counts, tool/file counts, and paired compaction count.
Each compaction is listed chronologically with exact token metadata when present.
The report explains that compaction remains in one transcript and does not mint a session ID.

evals.prompt: Create a deep lifetime view of this many-month Claude Code session. Include every historical compact summary in order, annotate the work between compactions, and add a fresh summary of the current head without touching the original session.
evals.expected_output: Uses the bundled deep-dive operation to combine local historical summaries with a current-head summary generated only on an isolated hidden fork.
assertions: Historical compact boundaries are paired to isCompactSummary records by UUID and emitted in transcript order.
Every epoch includes available timestamps, token metadata, prompt/assistant/tool counts, and explicit file read/change counts.
Only the current-head snapshot invokes Claude, using --resume with --fork-session in an isolated execution directory.
Source transcript integrity and picker membership are verified, and the print-mode fork is absent from picker indexes.
The current-head summary appears after all historical summaries.
